findings.title: No successful backup has ever run: every db-backup, storage-backup and db-restore-test CI run fails
evidence: GitHub Actions API (read-only, 2026-10-11): db-backup workflow 29/29 runs failed, 2026-06-06 through 2026-10-11; latest manual run 38106946181 failed in the 'Run database backup script' step in <1s; storage-backup 7/7 failed (latest 38046396647); db-restore-test 1/1 failed (37323743344); backup-dispatch latest 38046405190 fails at 'Require a dispatch token'
.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:14,21 — the job attaches `environment: dev` and injects `secrets.SUPABASE_DB_URL`; scripts/backup-database.sh:39-42 hard-fails when it is empty
.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:43-44 — `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` + `REQUIRE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION=1`; scripts/backup-database.sh:92-94 refuses to upload unencrypted when the key is absent
CHANGELOG.md:191-200 — 'Still required from the operator: SUPABASE_DB_URL, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the mainecybertech-backups bucket ...' (i.e. not provisioned at 8d299b8d)

docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:87-91 — the backup secrets are documented as Prod-only (Dev column '—') while the workflows run in `dev` (lines 110-114 acknowledge the dev environment but the table was not updated)
.github/workflows/backup-dispatch.yml:60-67 — the dispatcher fails loudly when SCHEDULE_DISPATCH_TOKEN is unset; the failing step confirms it is unset
docs/RELEASE_GATE.md:66-68 — release gate requires 'ordinary db-backup runs succeeding from the default branch' with a run URL as evidence; unmet
findings.impact: The platform has no long-term database backup and no storage mirror at any point in its history: the 30-day S3 recovery path, the weekly restore verification and the documented ≤24h dump RPO do not exist in practice. Only Supabase PITR (7-day, itself never exercised) could recover data; anything older or a lost/rotated Supabase project is unrecoverable. This is a release-blocking DR failure.
findings.recommendation: Operator: provision SUPABASE_DB_URL, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the backup bucket in the `dev` environment (or move the workflows to the environment that actually holds them) and set SCHEDULE_DISPATCH_TOKEN or retire the dispatcher; then run db-backup and db-restore-test manually and record the green run URLs in docs/RELEASE_GATE.md. Repo: correct docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md so the documented environment matches the workflows, and add a CI guard that fails fast with an actionable message when a required secret is missing.
findings.note: New finding this run. CI conclusions reproduced from the public GitHub Actions API (read-only); the exact log text is not retrievable unauthenticated, but the failing step completes in <1s — consistent with the script's first fail-closed check (SUPABASE_DB_URL) and with CHANGELOG.md:198. Orchestrator note: 'daily backups currently fail in CI (missing SUPABASE_DB_URL)'.

findings.title: The weekly restore test fails at baseline load (invalid GITHUB_ENV format) so no restore verification ever executes
evidence: .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:20-29 — 'Load restore-test baseline' runs `cat .github/restore-test-baseline.env >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`
.github/restore-test-baseline.env:1-28 — the file begins with 23 comment lines before the five KEY=VALUE floors (RESTORE_MIN_TABLES=120 etc.)

GitHub Actions run 37323743344 (2026-10-05, the only db-restore-test run): step 3 'Load restore-test baseline' failed; check-run annotations: Invalid format "# Baseline thresholds for .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml"; Unable to process file command 'env' successfully; steps 4-9 (Find latest backup, Download, Decrypt, Start temp PostgreSQL, Restore, Verify database integrity) were all skipped

git diff 5241a9be..8d299b8d -- .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml shows only the notifier block changed; the baseline-load step is byte-identical at HEAD, so the next scheduled run (Mon 2026-10-12) is expected to fail the same way
docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:74-75 — the baseline file is the definition of a 'verified' backup; docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:150-165 documents the same assertions for manual restores
findings.impact: The only automated proof that backups are recoverable cannot run: the integrity, freshness, tenant-scoping and RLS assertions added for DR-P0-002/IR-P1-004 are unreachable in CI, and release-gate item OBS-P2-003 (dated green db-restore-test) can never be met. A restore failure would not be detected by the drill.
findings.recommendation: Strip comments/blank lines before appending to $GITHUB_ENV (e.g. `grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' .github/restore-test-baseline.env >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`), or `set -a; . .github/restore-test-baseline.env; set +a` and write the values explicitly. Add a lint/unit test that every line written to $GITHUB_ENV is KEY=VALUE, and re-run the workflow to capture the first green run.
findings.note: New finding this run (introduced with the DR hardening commit bd086426, 2026-10-02; observed in the only scheduled run since).

findings.title: Storage backups can be silently partial or empty: listings are truncated at 1000 objects and a zero-object archive is accepted
evidence: scripts/backup-storage.sh:57-67 — list_paths posts a single `{"prefix":...,"limit":1000,"offset":0}` request and never paginates; a folder with >1000 direct children silently loses the remainder
scripts/backup-storage.sh:86-90 — walk_bucket recurses into folder entries but each list call still stops at 1000

scripts/backup-storage.sh:46,92-101 — OBJECT_COUNT is recorded in MANIFEST.txt but there is no comparison against a server-side total and no failure when OBJECT_COUNT=0; an empty archive uploads and reports success

scripts/backup-storage.sh:123 — the archive is uploaded without any size/count assertion (contrast scripts/backup-database.sh:57-74 which fails on a zero-byte dump and runs a VERIFY_BACKUP integrity check)
findings.impact: The storage mirror can report success while missing an unbounded number of uploaded documents; a restore during an incident would silently return a partial set of client files. There is no signal that distinguishes a complete archive from a truncated one.
findings.recommendation: Paginate the list endpoint until an empty page and compare the number of downloaded objects against the manifest/total; fail the job when OBJECT_COUNT is 0 or when the download count does not match the listing; add a `VERIFY_BACKUP`-equivalent check (tar -tzf the archive, assert MANIFEST present).
findings.note: New finding this run; no test exercises a >1000-object prefix.

findings.title: Storage backups are never restore-tested and the restore script asserts nothing
evidence: grep -rn 'restore-storage|storage-restore' .github/ — no matches: no CI job exercises the storage restore path (only db-restore-test.yml exists, and it covers the database)
scripts/restore-storage.sh:58-75,94-99 — downloads/extracts the newest archive and only prints MANIFEST.txt; it never asserts object_count, file counts, archive integrity or a checksum
scripts/restore-storage.sh:101-121 — uploads every extracted file and counts them, but the count is not validated against the manifest

docs/RTO_RPO.md:11,25 — claims storage RPO ≤24h via the daily mirror; docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:167-183 documents the restore path; no exercise artifact exists and all 7 storage-backup runs have failed
findings.impact: Recovery of uploaded documents/avatars/logos is unproven end-to-end; a corrupt or partial archive would only be discovered during an incident, after the source bucket state is already lost. The prompt's rule 'backups are insufficient unless restore is tested' applies directly.
findings.recommendation: Add a weekly storage restore-test job (mirroring db-restore-test.yml): fetch the newest archive into a throwaway environment, assert the MANIFEST object_count equals the extracted file count and the archive decrypts, and record a green run as the exercise artifact.
findings.note: New finding this run. Cross-reference: FILE-P2-004 (previous register) is superseded — the backup path now exists (DR-P1-001 verified-fixed) but is still not exercised.

findings.title: No independent backup-staleness alarm; notifier delivery failures are swallowed
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml — no backup/restore/staleness rule (grep -iE 'backup|restore|stale' returns only Watchdog comments); docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md has no backup section

.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:59-65, .github/workflows/storage-backup.yml:69-75, .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:252-258 — the notifiers end in `|| true` and have no `else`, so an unset/expired ntfy URL or a failed POST is silently ignored and the step still succeeds

The only signal that a backup stopped is the failing job itself (plus GitHub's own failure e-mail), i.e. the notification depends on the same run whose failure it reports — no out-of-band dead-man's switch exists (INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:124 already records the related IR-P0-003 gap for monitoring generally)
findings.impact: If the workflows are disabled, the cron is dropped, or the notifier credentials break, nobody is told; a silent backup gap is exactly the failure mode DR-P2-001 was raised for. The residual was not covered by the ntfy routing fix.
findings.recommendation: Add an independent 'no successful backup in 24/48h' check that does not depend on the backup job (external heartbeat service, or a Prometheus rule on a backup-success timestamp/metric), and make the notifier step fail (or emit ::error::) when no channel is configured instead of swallowing delivery errors.
findings.note: New finding this run; residual of DR-P2-001 (which is verified-fixed for ntfy delivery).

findings.title: Platform DR drill plan is only in a dated audit folder and the drill ledger is empty
evidence: docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:114,135 — reference `backup_restore_drill_plan.md` by bare name, but the only copy is docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/backup_restore_drill_plan.md; `secret_rotation_runbook.md` (lines 67,107,115) likewise exists only in that dated folder

findings.title: Database backups are unencrypted and stored in a single location with no offsite copy
evidence: scripts/backup-database.sh:76-97 — AES-256-CBC (PBKDF2) client-side encryption when BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, fail-closed with REQUIRE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION

docs/RTO_RPO.md:29-38 — operator actions outstanding (create the key, the offsite bucket, and exercise both)

GitHub Actions run 37323743344 — the 'Notify on failure' step ran and succeeded on the failed restore test

findings.title: No automated migration reverse/rollback and no bad-migration drill

findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: dry-run artifact + fail-closed post-push drift check + documented options; residual: no automated reverse migration, no recorded drill.

findings.title: RPO/RTO targets are documented but unvalidated, and the Postgres RPO conflates PITR with the daily dump

GitHub Actions: the freshness assertion has never executed (restore test 1/1 failed at baseline load); all 29 db-backup runs failed, so no dump exists to validate

findings.recommendation: Fix the restore-test baseline bug, get the dump path green, then record one dated PITR exercise and one dated dump-restore measurement; state which environment each number was measured in.

findings.title: Terraform state bucket versioning is claimed but not backed by any resource
evidence: docs/RTO_RPO.md:26 — 'Terraform state: DO Spaces (S3-compatible) with versioning enabled'
infra/terraform/digitalocean/providers.tf:6-19 — S3/Spaces backend with encrypt + use_lockfile, but no bucket resource anywhere in infra/terraform (grep 'spaces_bucket|digitalocean_spaces' → 0)

findings.impact: If versioning is not actually enabled (a manual Spaces API setting), a corrupted or wrongly-overwritten state file cannot be rolled back and the documented emergency path is fiction; the doc also points at the wrong bucket name.
findings.recommendation: Import/declare both state buckets as digitalocean_spaces_bucket resources with `versioning { enabled = true }` (DO Spaces supports it via API/provider), or record a verified manual setting with a check; correct the bucket name in ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md and add a state-restore drill (IR-P3-001).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (previously carried, not re-verified at 9c0b88c): claim unchanged and unbacked; new evidence that the emergency-restore doc names a different bucket than the backend config. DO docs confirm Spaces versioning + provider support.

findings.title: The backup/DR runbook and module docs describe a client-facing product, not the platform's own recovery, and the module doc is stale
evidence: docs/runbooks/backup-disaster-recovery.md:3-6 — scope banner added (bd086426): 'Scope: client-facing product module' with pointers to ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES §3a/§3b and RTO_RPO

docs/modules/backup-dr.md:22-32 — still documents /api/v1/backup-dr/jobs|dr-tests|dashboard|export; the implemented surface is /api/v1/final/backups* (apps/api/src/routes/final.ts:6,17; final/crud.ts:177)
docs/modules/backup-dr.md:36 — documents backup_jobs/backup_results/dr_tests tables; migration supabase/migrations/5302075_backup_dr.sql:2-31 creates only backup_status
findings.impact: Partially fixed: the runbook now warns it is the product module, but the module doc still sends readers to endpoints and tables that do not exist.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite docs/modules/backup-dr.md against the real /final/backups* surface and backup_status schema (or delete the stale sections); add a doc/route existence check.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: runbook banner present; module doc still stale (endpoint drift tracked separately as DR-P3-003).

findings.title: Manual restore has no environment guardrail and the transient dump is written unencrypted to `/tmp`
evidence: scripts/restore-database.sh:54-63 — non-local targets are refused unless ALLOW_PROD_RESTORE=yes (added bd086426)
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:143-145 — guardrail documented
scripts/restore-database.sh:69,86,101,115 — the dump is still staged as plaintext /tmp/restore.sql.gz and piped to psql; no secure-delete or encrypted temp storage
findings.impact: Partially fixed: the prod-overwrite guardrail is in place; the transient plaintext copy of tenant data remains on the operator host during a restore.
findings.recommendation: Decrypt-and-stream directly into psql (or use an encrypted temp volume) and shred the temp file on every exit path; keep the ALLOW_PROD_RESTORE gate.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: guardrail present; plaintext /tmp staging unchanged.

findings.title: The product `backup_status` module is not wired to any real platform backup heartbeat
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:278-331 — backupDrCheck reads/updates backup_status rows by age only (RPO/RTO columns unused); scheduled in apps/worker/src/schedule-config.ts:39
Only demo seeds insert rows: supabase/migrations/5302120_demo_module_data.sql:599, 5302123_demo_expanded_test_data.sql:296
No writer derives backup_status from .github/workflows/db-backup.yml; no platform heartbeat table or metric exists (grep backup_status writers / 'backup' in apps/api routes)
findings.impact: The only in-app backup monitor watches seeded client data, so the platform's own failing daily backup is invisible to it. Compounded by the new P0: every backup run fails and nothing in the product surface reflects it.
findings.recommendation: Record the last successful platform backup (small heartbeat table or metric) and alert on staleness; keep the client-facing module separate and clearly labelled.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (previously carried, not re-verified at 9c0b88c): unchanged.

findings.title: Duplicate backup-script logic in bash and PowerShell risks drift
evidence: scripts/backup-database.ps1:18-24 — 'NOT CANONICAL' header added (bd086426): CI uses the bash script; the PS helper does not encrypt and has no offsite copy
scripts/backup-database.ps1:75-132 vs scripts/backup-database.sh:44-135 — duplicate dump/upload/prune flow remains, with divergent retention (bulk delete-objects vs per-object) and no encryption path
findings.impact: Partially fixed: the canonical script is now documented, but the duplicate logic remains and will diverge further (it can never produce an encrypted/offsite backup).
findings.recommendation: Make the PowerShell helper delegate to the bash script (WSL/Git Bash) or delete it; if kept, add a parity test/checklist.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: canonical note added; duplicate logic still present.

findings.title: Unpinned Postgres image in the restore test; no explicit jq/aws tool pinning in the backup job
evidence: .github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:112-116 — `docker run ... postgres:16-alpine` (floating tag)
scripts/backup-database.sh:45-50 — pg_dump client version is runner-provided or the postgres:15 container (unpinned)
Also tracked as CI-P3-007 in the CI area

evidence: docs/modules/backup-dr.md:22-32 — documents GET /api/v1/backup-dr/jobs|dr-tests|dashboard|export

findings.recommendation: Update docs/modules/backup-dr.md to the real routes and mark the export as not implemented (or implement it); add a doc/route consistency check.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d (previously carried, not re-verified at 9c0b88c): unchanged.

findings.title: Terraform state restore guidance lacks a tested procedure
evidence: docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:214-223 — 'Restore previous Terraform state (emergency)' gives no procedure beyond 'Restore from a prior version via DO Spaces UI or CLI' and names bucket 'mct-portal-tfstate-<env>'
infra/terraform/digitalocean/env/backend.dev.hcl:5 / backend.prod.hcl:5 — actual buckets are portal-terraform-state-development / -production
No versioning resource (DR-P2-002) and no state-restore drill record (docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:114 all _pending_)
findings.impact: An emergency state restore would have to be improvised against an unversioned (unverified) bucket with the wrong name in the doc.
findings.recommendation: Correct the bucket names, document the exact version-restore commands, and run a state-restore drill (D6) recording the result.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d as a subject-in-DR row (IR-P3-001, cross-area): no tested procedure; bucket-name drift found this run. Also covered by the DR-P2-002 remediation.

report:
# Backup and Restore Drill Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive (full hardening rerun)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`

## Executive Summary

The DR tooling is far better documented and coded than at the original audit — encryption, offsite copy, destination contract, restore assertions, failure alerts and rollback docs all exist. **None of it has ever worked in practice.** Every CI run of the database backup (29/29 since 2026-06-06), the storage mirror (7/7) and the restore test (1/1) has failed; the dispatcher that was supposed to make the schedules fire fails because `SCHEDULE_DISPATCH_TOKEN` is unset. The repo itself records why: `CHANGELOG.md:191-200` lists `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and the backup bucket as "still required from the operator", and `docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:87-91` still documents those secrets as Prod-only even though the workflows now attach `environment: dev` — a contract mismatch that guarantees the jobs cannot resolve their configuration.

Three new defects compound the picture: the weekly restore test fails before it can verify anything because it appends a commented `.env` file to `$GITHUB_ENV` (runner rejects it as "Invalid format"), so the integrity assertions added for DR-P0-002 are unreachable; the storage mirror silently truncates listings at 1000 objects per prefix and accepts a zero-object archive; and no independent "no recent backup" alarm exists (the notifiers swallow delivery errors with `|| true`).

Net state: the platform has **no long-term backup of any kind**, the documented 30-day S3 recovery path and ≤24h dump RPO are fiction, and only Supabase PITR (7-day, never exercised) remains as a possible recovery path. Recommended next actions: (1) provision the backup secrets in the environment the workflows actually use (or move the workflows) and record green `db-backup` + `db-restore-test` run URLs; (2) fix the baseline-load step (one-line grep); (3) add the storage restore test and pagination/count guards.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Database backup workflow and script

- Evidence: `db-backup.yml:14,21,43-44`; `backup-database.sh:39-42,52-61,66-74,76-97,103,106-111,118-135`.
- What it does: daily (04:00 UTC) `pg_dump | gzip` → optional AES-256-CBC → `aws s3 cp` (STANDARD_IA) → optional offsite copy → 30-day prune; fails on missing URL, zero-byte dump and (with `REQUIRE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION=1`) missing key.
- How it appears to work: complete and fail-closed; it is the only path that would produce a long-term backup.
- Dependencies: `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, Spaces keys, bucket, `pg_dump`, `aws`, `jq`.
- Current controls: fail-closed checks, encryption, offsite affordance, retention, failure notifier.
- Missing controls: provisioned secrets; a green run; an independent staleness alarm.
- Risks: P0 — no backup exists; RPO unbounded beyond PITR.
- Recommended improvement: provision `SUPABASE_DB_URL` + `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `dev` (or move the workflow to the environment that holds them), fix the secrets matrix, run it green.
- Suggested tests: a CI guard test that asserts required secrets exist before the schedule matters; a synthetic bad-URL run that fails and alerts.
- Suggested docs: correct `GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md`; add the green run URL to `RELEASE_GATE.md`.
